gold_answer:
You need to understand how [ ` useEffect `
](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffect) and [ state
](https://react.dev/learn/state-a-components-memory) is supposed to be used in
React.

  1. You should not rely on _when_ or how often ` useEffect ` is executed. You should only use it to declare which state depends on which other state (see also [ "You Might Not Need an Effect" ](https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect) ). 

  2. The "state" from ` setState ` (the value and the ` set... ` function) should be used to e.g. update based on some other state or on user actions. It should not be used like a normal "variable". 

> When you call ` useState ` , you are telling React that you want this
> component to remember something

Note that the complete ` for ` loop runs until it is finished **before** React
even tries to execute ` setCurrentDeck ` . When the ` for ` loop is finished,
all ` set... ` functions are executed, which is effectively like only the last
one was executed.

###  Maybe a solution:

I suppose you probably should build the new deck using "normal" javascript
patterns (maybe in a separate function), i.e. without using React specific
patterns. Then, when the deck is created and it's time to interact with the
user and update the screen again, update the React state with the ready built
deck.
